results.note: Recording (New Focus 2017) titles it 'No. N in <key>' as in our title. 1667 is the Vincenti print (RISM R 2565); IMSLP's ca.1660 composition date is an estimate, so the house fallback (publication year) stays. Recorded 6.9 min.

Same print and recording; 7.3 min.
Murray D6 = Quartet Op. 4/1 in A (Wikipedia work list); Gramola disc (Demmler Quartet) calls it Op. 2 No. 1, movements and 16.6 min match.
Murray D16 = Flute Quartet in G; Compagnia di Punto, DHM 2013: three movements, 15.6 min.

B27 is Kaul I:58 (orchestral series) and the Amadeus (Scheck) edition is for 2 flutes, 2 horns and string orchestra; the other recording (CPO) is orchestral. The one-to-a-part claim (nine players on the DHM disc) rests on a PDF review I could not read, and MusicBrainz lists only the ensemble. Notes say 'framed by marches' but the DHM tracks show only one March (first movement). Possibly string-orchestra scope; keep only if a one-to-a-part source is found
1925 is the Muzgiz publication year (IMSLP); Wikipedia and IMSLP's work list date the composition 1921. One movement, 13.8-14.8 min on two recordings.

Year was blank: IMSLP's scan is the St Petersburg Society for Jewish Folk Music edition of 1914, which is the house fallback. Toccata Classics (Russian Jewish Classics Vol. 4) plays it in 10.0 min; scoring violin, cello, piano per IMSLP.
Libro 3 (1613) No. 2; complete Tactus recording 4.3 min, Pan Classics 'Sonata Seconda' 4.2 min.

IMSLP: 15 sinfonie a 3, 12 pieces a 4-5; title page says two viole or two cornetti and chitarrone. Recorded only in selections (Sinfonia decima on Pan Classics, others per MusicBrainz); kept as a set.

IMSLP's 'viols' tag rests on the title 'due viole'; Rossi's 1613 title says 'viole da braccio' and the 1622 one 'violini', and the canto parts are treble, so two violins stays (a modern edition note says Libro 1 suggests violins or cornetti). Recorded only in selections (Sinfonia 17, Pan Classics).
Nonetto 1959, rev. 1974 and 1977 (Wikipedia list); five movements; recordings 24.6-30.6 min.
Quintetto 1935; three movements, 16.1 and 14.6 min; also on the ASV Ex Novo Ensemble disc.

Quartetto 1948-54; movements Allegro moderato, Adagio non troppo, Allegro robusto; full recording by Ex Novo Ensemble (ASV DCA 1072, per MusicWeb and MusicBrainz), about 14 min.
Wikipedia: 'Quartetto d'archi con voce (1929)'; BIS (Kremer) 6.8 min.
